classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports an attempted double-free of a 5-byte text buffer, first freed from `xsltEvalTemplateString` and freed again while `xsltFreeStylesheet` tears down `style->doc`.

bug_description.normalized: The exact staged `poc` is parsed by `xsltFuzzXslt` with `xmlReadMemory(data, size, NULL, NULL, 0)`, so the leading `&a;` inside `<x:template match="*">` remains an `XML_ENTITY_REF_NODE` instead of being consumed by `XML_PARSE_NOENT`. During `xsltParseStylesheetUser`, vulnerable `xsltPreprocessStylesheet` inspects only `cur->children->type`; because the template's first child is that entity-reference node, the guard at `libxslt/xslt.c:3658-3663` refuses to descend into any of the template children. The preprocessor therefore never reaches the later `<x:message><x:attribute name="n">   o</x:attribute></x:message>` subtree, never internalizes the 5-byte heap buffer for `"   o"`, and still leaves `style->internalized` true. At transform time `xsltNewTransformContext` copies that stale invariant into `ctxt->internalized`, `xsltEvalTemplateString` builds a temporary node for `xsl:message`, and `xsltAttribute` takes its single-text fast path, executing `copyTxt->content = inst->children->content` instead of duplicating the attribute text. Freeing the temporary node in `xsltEvalTemplateString` releases the aliased buffer once; later `xsltFreeStylesheet` calls `xmlFreeDoc(style->doc)`, and `xmlFreeNodeList` frees the same original stylesheet text buffer again. AddressSanitizer reports the crash at `libxml2/tree.c:3721`, the previous free rooted at `libxslt/templates.c:253`, and the allocation rooted at `libxml2/SAX2.c:1878`. The fix removes the entity-child skip so preprocessing descends into that subtree and internalizes or deletes the relevant nodes before transformation.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the attacker buffer. The fuzz helper parses the exact witness into an XML stylesheet document with parser options `0`, which preserves the leading entity reference and materializes the later attribute-text node used on the vulnerable path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact no-newline stylesheet string `<!DOCTYPEF[<!ENTITY a ''>]><x:stylesheet xmlns:x="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"><x:template match="*">&a;<x:message><x:attribute name="n">   o</x:attribute></x:message></x:template></x:stylesheet>`. Because `xmlReadMemory` is called with options `0`, the leading `&a;` remains a parsed entity-reference child ahead of the later `xsl:message/xsl:attribute` subtree instead of being pre-expanded by `XML_PARSE_NOENT`.
source.note: This is the first project statement that consumes `data,size`. The later root cause depends on the parsed DOM shape created here, not on the libFuzzer entry point.

sink.description: ASan sink. While `xmlFreeDoc(style->doc)` walks the original stylesheet tree, `xmlFreeNodeList` frees the text node content buffer a second time.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: attempting double-free` at `xmlFreeNodeList` line 3721, with the previous free rooted at `xsltEvalTemplateString` line 253 and the crash path entered from `xsltFreeStylesheet` line 1075.

root_cause.description: Broken child-walk logic. If an element's first child is an entity declaration/reference/node, preprocessing refuses to descend into that element's child list, so later siblings in the same subtree are skipped as well.
root_cause.note: For the witness template, `cur->children` is the leading `&a;` entity-reference node. This leaves the later `xsl:message/xsl:attribute` text subtree unvisited and uninternalized while `style->internalized` stays true. The fix commit removes the `XML_ENTITY_DECL` / `XML_ENTITY_REF_NODE` / `XML_ENTITY_NODE` exclusions so preprocessing always descends.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete heap buffer later freed twice. Parsing `<x:attribute name="n">   o</x:attribute>` stores the attribute-text bytes in a fresh text-node content allocation here.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The witness attribute body is exactly three spaces followed by `o`, so this allocation produces the 5-byte region `"   o\0"` that AddressSanitizer later reports.
tainted_value_origin.note: This is the same allocation chain reported in the staged ASan trace (`xmlStrndup` -> `xmlSAX2TextNode`).

parser_admitted.description: The parsed attacker stylesheet is handed to libxslt's stylesheet parser/preprocessor. The later transformation and stylesheet cleanup prove this call succeeds on the staged witness.
parser_admitted.note: This is the entry from the fuzz helper into the vulnerable stylesheet-compilation path.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact witness is parsed into a stylesheet DOM with default XML parser options, which preserves `&a;` as the first child of the template and allocates the `xsl:attribute` text `"   o"` on the heap.

Because the template's first child is an entity-reference node, vulnerable preprocessing skips the entire template child list, leaving the later `xsl:message/xsl:attribute` subtree unvisited while the stylesheet still claims to be fully internalized.
Transformation setup copies the stale internalized flag into `ctxt`, creates an output document reusing `ctxt->dict`, and `xsl:message` evaluation builds a temporary node in that output document.
The witness `xsl:attribute` has a single text child, so the single-text fast path aliases the original stylesheet text buffer into the temporary message attribute instead of duplicating it.

Freeing the temporary message node releases the aliased buffer once, and later `xsltFreeStylesheet` -> `xmlFreeDoc(style->doc)` frees the same original stylesheet text buffer again, producing the ASan double-free.

fine_trace.note: Source. The exact staged stylesheet is parsed from the attacker buffer with options `0`, not `XML_PARSE_NOENT`. That DOM keeps the template's leading `&a;` as an entity-reference node and contains the later `xsl:message/xsl:attribute` subtree whose text becomes the double-freed buffer.

While parsing `<x:attribute name="n">   o</x:attribute>`, libxml2 allocates a heap-backed text buffer for `"   o"`. The ASan allocation report shows a 5-byte region, exactly matching those 4 visible characters plus the NUL terminator.

Root cause. When preprocessing the witness `<x:template>`, `cur->children` is the leading `XML_ENTITY_REF_NODE` for `&a;`, so this guard refuses to descend into any template children. The loop therefore never reaches the entity node to delete it and never reaches the later `xsl:message/xsl:attribute` text node from step 2 to internalize it, yet `style->internalized` remains true.

After stylesheet parsing succeeds, the transform context copies the stale `style->internalized` flag into `ctxt->internalized`. The transformation now assumes stylesheet text nodes are dict-owned even though step 3 left step 2's buffer heap-owned.

The result document for this transformation reuses `ctxt->dict` and becomes `ctxt->output`. Temporary nodes created during `xsl:message` evaluation therefore live in a document whose `dict` matches `ctxt->dict`.

While executing the witness `xsl:message`, libxslt creates a temporary `insert` node in `ctxt->output`, makes it the current insertion target, and evaluates the message child list on that temporary node. In the witness, that child list contains the single `xsl:attribute name="n">   o</x:attribute>` instruction.

The witness `xsl:attribute` has exactly one text child, so `xsltAttribute` takes the single-text fast path. Because step 4 made `ctxt->internalized` true and steps 5-6 place `ctxt->insert` in a document whose `dict` equals `ctxt->dict`, the fast path aliases the original stylesheet text buffer from step 2 into the temporary attribute node instead of duplicating it.

This is the first free. When `xsl:message` finishes, `xsltEvalTemplateString` frees the temporary `insert` tree. Because step 7 made the temporary attribute text node alias step 2's buffer, `xmlFreeNode(insert)` releases that heap buffer once here through `xmlFreePropList` and `xmlFreeNodeList`.

Later stylesheet teardown still frees `style->doc`. Because step 3 never processed the template subtree, the original stylesheet text node still owns the same buffer that step 8 already freed, so document cleanup starts a second free pass over that stale ownership state.

Sink. `xmlFreeNodeList` reaches the original stylesheet text node and frees `cur->content` again. That `cur->content` is the same 5-byte `"   o\0"` buffer allocated in step 2 and already released at step 8, so AddressSanitizer reports the crashing double-free at this line.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack points to `xmlStrndup` called from `xmlSAX2TextNode`. The witness text `"   o"` is 4 characters, so the reported 5-byte region size matches this allocation exactly.

free_context.note: ASan's previous-free stack reaches `xsltEvalTemplateString` line 253. Freeing the temporary `insert` node there triggers `xmlFreeNode` -> `xmlFreePropList` -> `xmlFreeNodeList`, which releases the aliased attribute-text buffer the first time.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation stack reports a 5-byte `xmlSAX2TextNode` text allocation, which exactly matches the witness `xsl:attribute` body `"   o"`. The fine trace shows vulnerable preprocessing skipping that subtree because the template's first child is `&a;`, leaving the buffer heap-owned while `style->internalized` stays true; later `xsltAttribute` aliases that same buffer into the temporary message attribute before `xmlFreeNodeList` frees it again during stylesheet teardown.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is the exact one-line stylesheet text `<!DOCTYPEF[<!ENTITY a ''>]><x:stylesheet xmlns:x="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"><x:template match="*">&a;<x:message><x:attribute name="n">   o</x:attribute></x:message></x:template></x:stylesheet>`. Parsed by `xsltFuzzXslt` through `xmlReadMemory(data, size, NULL, NULL, 0)`, it produces a template whose first child is the entity reference `&a;` and whose later `xsl:attribute` text is `"   o"`; that exact layout triggers the skipped-preprocessing subtree, the aliasing fast path, and the double-free.

format.name: One-line XSLT stylesheet text for tests/fuzz/xslt
format.contract: Exactly the staged `poc` file as parsed by `xsltFuzzXslt` with `xmlReadMemory(..., 0)`. The verified trigger is not generalized beyond this witness: it must preserve the leading `&a;` as the first child of the template and preserve the single text child `"   o"` inside `xsl:message` -> `xsl:attribute`, because those exact source-level facts are what make `xsltPreprocessStylesheet` skip the subtree and later make `xsltAttribute` alias the same text buffer into the temporary message node.
